public_rationale: The forecast has no deadline, and no decisive event satisfying the resolution rule was established. Prospective contract economics offer countercontext, but do not prove realized recovery of GPU costs. Continued spending or a failure to recover costs so far would not establish 'never'. The undefined GPU population and accounting basis also prevent a firm financial verdict.
limitations: Projected payback and annualized revenue are not realized recovery.
An isolated buyer's results would not necessarily settle a claim about the aggregate purchase population.
The unknown accounting basis bars a supported or contradicted financial score.

conditions: these GPUs (those under discussion in his NVIDIA analysis)

statement.excerpt: how AI revenues will never pay back the cost of these GPUs

our_interpretation: Read 'these GPUs' as the NVIDIA GPUs bought for AI discussed in the referenced analysis, rather than every future GPU.
The ordinary revenue-based reading compares cumulative realized AI revenue attributable to those purchases with their acquisition costs.
Do not substitute profit, EBITDA, annualized revenue or signed contract value for realized revenue.
The reference to 'these GPUs' identifies an asset population; it is not a conditional antecedent.
No deadline is stated, so the forecast has an open horizon.
criteria.support_condition: For an identified purchase population, final lifetime AI revenue remains below acquisition cost after the GPUs are retired and no further attributable receipts can arise.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Documented cumulative realized AI revenue attributable to the same identified purchase population reaches or exceeds its acquisition cost.
